 Caldwell Sheriff Announces New Look, Key Deadline Reminders for Property Tax Bills
 by 
 Tammy Hancock 
 October 19, 2026 
 At Tuesday’s fiscal court meeting, Sheriff Don Weedman outlined changes residents will see on this year’s property tax bills.
 Weedman said tax bills will be mailed around November 1 and will look different than in past years. Instead of postcards, the bills will now be letter-sized. He said the change was needed because of problems with postcards, including issues with post office boxes and postal equipment. The new format is designed to be easier to read and easier for residents to return with payment.
 https://dehayf5mhw1h7.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/sites/2264/2026/10/18183011/Wireready_10-18-2026-18-30-10_A120_20261018182949801-1.mp3 
 click to download audio Residents will receive a 2% discount if they pay during November. Bills paid in December will be at face value. After that, penalties will begin to increase.
 Weedman said the deadline rules will be applied fairly. He noted that the drop box is checked at midnight on deadline dates, including November 30 for the discount period and New Year’s for the face amount deadline.
 The sheriff also said the back of the tax bill will include an address change form. Residents who need to update their mailing address can fill out and sign the form, which will then be used to make the correction through the Property Valuation Administrator’s office.
 The bill will also include a website where residents can check their tax status at any time.
 https://dehayf5mhw1h7.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/sites/2264/2026/10/18183012/Wireready_10-18-2026-18-30-10_A120_20261018182949801-2.mp3 
 click to download audio Weedman also reminded residents that beginning April 1, the sheriff’s office will no longer accept personal checks for tax payments. He said bad checks can create problems with collections and auditing.
 Another reminder included residents who may qualify for the Homestead Exemption.
 https://dehayf5mhw1h7.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/sites/2264/2026/10/18183012/Wireready_10-18-2026-18-30-10_A120_20261018182949801-3.mp3 
 click to download audio Weedman also praised the employees who handle tax collections, saying they work professionally with the public and with other county offices during what can sometimes be a stressful time of year.
